transcript.content: Build a small editable specimen-board exporter for our SVG board utility. Board input and editing interaction are undecided.
Source offer offer-620a6956-1b41-4a44-acf0-b6a86beb307f: What board kind and editing model should the first slice support, and how strict should validation of the board input be?

sourceOffers.scope: A small editable specimen-board exporter for our SVG board utility, limited to: (1) loading a board from an input format, (2) basic editing of board contents, (3) exporting a specimen board. Deliberately excludes any GUI design, framework choice, or persistence backend until the decisions below are made.
sourceOffers.question: What board kind and editing model should the first slice support, and how strict should validation of the board input be?

options.label: Rectangular grid board, strict validation
options.tradeoff: Smallest, most predictable first slice: the board is a fixed rectangular grid of cells, input is validated up front and rejected with clear errors, and editing is cell-by-cell. Costs: cannot represent irregular or freeform boards until a later slice; some input sources will be rejected that a lenient parser would accept.
options.acceptanceExample: Given a JSON input describing a 8x6 grid of cells with labels, loading succeeds; loading input where one row has 7 cells fails with "row 4 has 7 cells, expected 8"; editing a cell label and exporting produces an SVG specimen-board reflecting the edit.

source.quote: Build a small editable specimen-board exporter for our SVG board utility. Board input and editing interaction are undecided.

options.label: Freely-placed items board, lenient parsing
options.tradeoff: Supports irregular boards: the board is a set of items with positions/sizes rather than a grid, and parsing accepts partial or malformed data by applying defaults and recording warnings. Costs: harder to validate, exports can silently differ from uploader intent, and editing needs a spatial interaction model rather than simple cell addressing.
options.acceptanceExample: Given input with items at coordinates, loading succeeds even if one item is missing a size (default applied with a warning); editing an item's position and exporting produces an SVG reflecting the new position; export log lists all applied warnings.

source.quote: Build a small editable specimen-board exporter for our SVG board utility. Board input and editing interaction are undecided.

options.label: Grid first with an item abstraction reserved
options.tradeoff: Start with the strict rectangular grid (cheapest to validate and edit) but internally model the board as a list of positioned items, so a freer board kind can be added later without an export rewrite. Costs: slightly more abstraction up front than the strict-grid-only slice, and the second board kind itself remains undecided, not promised.
options.acceptanceExample: Given the same 8x6 grid input as the strict option, all strict-option acceptance behaviors hold; additionally the export routine never branches on "is grid" but on the board's item list, verified by a second board kind producing the same SVG path in a later slice (not tested here).
